after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Which of the following represents a reflection across the $x$-axis?
after.worked_solution:
The correct answer is $T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].$ Indeed, consider the standard basis ${i,j}$ of the Euclidean plane ${R}^{2}$ and the unit square spanned by the vectors, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14067709/assets/9e322e6ed1ddb8f1d094633e931cd179b7eb9d6f47acd7c7d0809f113df91b22.png)

Now, we can find the images of ${i,j}$ under $T$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =T(i)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=i \\ {j}^{′} & =T(j)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-j\end{aligned}
$$

We can write $T(v)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =[\begin{aligned}56 \\ -98\end{aligned}] \\  & =14\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =14v\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $T(v)=14v,$ and so the linear transformation $T$ is a dilation with scale factor $k=14.$

The matrix that represents a dilation of scale factor $k$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 0 \\ 0 & k\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the standard matrix of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}14 & 0 \\ 0 & 14\end{aligned}].
$$

$$

The matrix that represents a dilation of scale factor $k$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 0 \\ 0 & k\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the standard matrix of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}].
$$
